- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is flat or rising, force a downward correction, especially after recent spikes.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or adjust downward by 5–10% for next 5 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and history shows mean reversion, model often overcorrects — apply a 3–5% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- If true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average instead of 30-day.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is weak or mixed, reduce forecast growth rate by 15–20% to account for volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ negative entries), model tends to ignore them — apply a 5–10% downward bias to forecast.
